title: Evaluation of the Integration of Learning Management Systems with Virtual Reality Platform
reason: Re-extraction. VR-in-LMS usage metrics (time in VR, completion rate, modules completed) correlated with post-test retention (r = 0.62, 0.45, 0.33). Meets I1, but sample is government-institution employees in professional training: E3 risk flagged.

extraction.design: mixed methods: Pearson correlation, t-test, ANOVA, multiple regression, CFA, interviews
extraction.n_quote: A ... total of 200 participants from various Indonesian government institutions took part ... in a one-month professional training program
extraction.population: employees of Indonesian government institutions in a one-month professional training programme (not HE students)
extraction.lms_indicators: time spent in VR (minutes/day), module completion rate (%), number of modules completed, training duration (days); system-generated
extraction.outcome_or_construct: knowledge retention (post-test score %); SDT motivation (autonomy, competence, relatedness; self-report)

effect_sizes.between: time spent in VR (minutes/day) ↔ post-test retention score
effect_sizes.quote: Time spent in VR 0.62 0.000 Moderate to strong

effect_sizes.between: module completion rate ↔ post-test retention score
number of modules completed ↔ post-test retention score
VR duration ↔ retention score, adjusted for autonomy and engagement scores
effect_sizes.quote: VR duration emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.41, p < 0.001)

extraction.notes: Three Table 2 cells change: country Indonesia (not nr); effect size reported (r = 0.62 strongest); 'object-interaction frequency' is not measured anywhere in the text (indicators are time in VR, completion rate, modules completed). E3: participants are government employees, which brief_2b lists as a non-qualifying sample. The manuscript's narrative ('personality scales') does not match: constructs are SDT motivation and engagement, used as co-predictors, not related to the VR metrics. Completion-rate data for 160 of 200 (Table 4); ANOVA F(2, 187) implies 190 cases; regression R2 not reported. Consistency check (not an estimate): the Table 5 p-values do not fit the stated N. With N = 160-200, r = 0.45 and r = 0.33 would give p far below 0.001, yet the paper reports p = 0.001 and p = 0.015; the correlations' N is never stated. Treat the r values with caution.

table2_current.lms_indicators: Time in VR environment, object-interaction frequency
